Variants.Content: During the invasion of Poland in 1241, Wrocław faced approaching forces. Castle, settlement and countryside offered differing protection. Moving people, animals and grain depended on roads, gate arrangements and available carts.

During the invasion of Poland in 1241, Wrocław faced approaching forces. Castle, settlement and countryside offered differing protection. Moving people, animals and grain depended on roads, gate arrangements and available carts. Defenders rotated rest, watches and repairs, while sorties exposed those outside. Besiegers also needed food and fodder; weather and delay burdened both sides.

During the invasion of Poland in 1241, Wrocław faced approaching forces. Castle, settlement and countryside offered differing protection. Moving people, animals and grain depended on roads, gate arrangements and available carts. Commanders weighed stores, relief and endurance before holding or negotiating. A promised army was not a delivered grain cart, and repaired walls did not replace food.

During the invasion of Poland in 1241, Wrocław faced approaching forces. Castle, settlement and countryside offered differing protection. Moving people, animals and grain depended on roads, gate arrangements and available carts. Families allocated food, water and shelter from fire, burdening hosts in crowded quarters. Refugees still worried over abandoned fields, animals and houses.
